brief:
Netanyahu's Likud-led bloc has slipped to 55 seats in the latest count, Middle East Eye reported, leaving the Israeli prime minister's coalition short of the 61-seat majority needed to form a government. The bloc had previously held 56 seats, marking another erosion of support in recent polling.

The decline reflects ongoing volatility in Israeli politics as negotiations for a governing coalition continue. Netanyahu remains positioned as the leading political force despite the setback, though he will require additional partners to reach a working majority in parliament.
dek: Netanyahu's bloc leads at 55 seats, but short of majority vote Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc has had a further decrease in seats, from 56 to 55, but remains in the lead.
title: Netanyahu's bloc loses ground to 55 seats, falls short of majority
